paragraphs.en: The old man introduced his cousin as his wife, whom he had married when he was young and she was twelve. They lived together for thirty years without children. Despite this, he continued to treat her kindly.
paragraphs.zh: 这位老人把他的堂姐介绍为自己的妻子，他年轻时娶了她，当时她才十二岁。他们一起生活了三十年，却没有孩子。尽管如此，他对她依然很好。

paragraphs.en: One day, he took a mistress who bore him a son resembling the moon. His wife grew jealous and, while he was away on a journey, cast spells on both his son and his wife, transforming them into a young bull and a cow respectively. She then gave the bull to their shepherd to tend with the other cattle.
paragraphs.zh: 有一天，他纳了一个妾，为他生下一个像月亮般俊美的儿子。妻子见状嫉妒不已，在他外出旅行期间，对父子二人施了咒术，将他们分别变成了公牛和母牛。随后，她把公牛交给牧人，与其它牛一起照料。

paragraphs.en: After my mistress died and my son ran away two months ago, I mourned for them deeply. As the Great Feast of the Immolation approached, I asked the shepherd to bring me a fat cow for sacrifice. The cow turned out to be my enchanted mistress.
paragraphs.zh: 自从我的女主人两个月前去世，而我的儿子也逃之夭夭后，我深深地为他们哀悼。临近献祭盛会的日子，我请牧羊人给我带来一头肥牛作为牺牲品。没想到那头牛竟是我那位施了魔法的女主人。

paragraphs.en: When I tried to kill her, she pleaded, "My son, my son," and cried tears that ran down her cheeks. Pitying her, I stopped and asked the shepherd for another cow. My wife urged me to proceed, saying we should enjoy her meat at the feast.
paragraphs.zh: 当我试图杀她时，她哀求道：“我的儿子，我的儿子。”眼泪顺着她的脸颊滚落。出于怜悯，我停了下来，并向牧羊人请求再要一头牛。妻子催促我继续，说我们应该在宴会上享受她的肉食。

paragraphs.en: Despite her cries, I ordered the shepherd to butcher her. When he skinned her, only skin and bone remained. Regretting my actions, I told him to take her or give her away and find a young bull instead.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管她不停地呼救，我还是命令牧羊人将她宰杀了。等他剥去她的皮后，只剩下一副骨架。事后我感到后悔，便吩咐他把她带走或者送给别人，并另找一头年轻的公牛来代替。

paragraphs.en: The shepherd left, and I never learned what happened to her.
paragraphs.zh: 牧羊人走了，我再也没有得知她的下落。

paragraphs.en: The old man brought his son, a young bull, before me. The boy broke free from the rope, ran to me, and threw himself at my feet, rubbing his head against mine as tears streamed down his cheeks. I was moved by this sight and told the shepherd to let him go with the flock.
paragraphs.zh: 老汉领着他的儿子，一头健壮的小公牛，来到我面前。那孩子挣脱了绳索，跑向我，扑到我的脚边，头抵着我的腿，泪水顺着脸颊滚落。这一幕让我动容，便让牧羊人放他和羊群一起回去。

paragraphs.en: My wife insisted on sacrificing the bull, but I refused, saying I had decided to spare it.
paragraphs.zh: 但我妻子坚持要献祭公牛，我坚决拒绝了，说我已经决定要放它一马。

paragraphs.en: Dawn broke, and Shahrazad fell silent, leaving the king eager for more. Her sister Dinarzad commented, "What an engaging story!" Shahrazad replied, "Tomorrow night, I will share something even stranger."
paragraphs.zh: 黎明来临，沙赫拉兹德停下了讲述，国王不禁渴望听到更多。她的妹妹丁尔扎德评论道：“真是个引人入胜的故事！”沙赫拉兹德回答说：“明天晚上，我会给大家讲一个更奇怪的故事。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Dinarzad urged her sister: "Please, tell us one of your tales." Shahrazad agreed with pleasure.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，迪纳扎德催促她的妹妹：“求你了，给我们讲一个你的故事吧。”沙赫拉兹德欣然应允。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad then recounted how the old man spoke to a demon and his companions.
paragraphs.zh: 莎赫拉兹接着讲述了那位老人与一个恶魔及其同伴交谈的情景。

paragraphs.en: I took the knife but hesitated as my son pleaded with tears and cries. He rolled at my feet, and with his tongue, he motioned toward me. Suspecting something amiss, I grew wary and pitied him.
paragraphs.zh: 我拿起刀子，却在儿子泪眼婆娑的哀求下犹豫不决。他滚到我的脚边，用舌头指了指自己。我察觉有些不对劲，变得警惕起来，同时心中也生出几分怜悯。

paragraphs.en: Finally, I released him, telling my wife, "I have decided to spare him; you take care of him." To appease her, I slaughtered another bull and promised to do the same for our son next season.
paragraphs.zh: 最后，我放过了他，并对妻子说：“我决定饶了它；你好好照顾它。”为了安抚她的情绪，我又宰了一头牛，并承诺在下一个季节为我们的儿子做同样的事情。

paragraphs.en: That night, we slept peacefully. When dawn broke, the shepherd arrived unannounced. He said, "I bring good news."
paragraphs.zh: 那个晚上，我们睡得很安稳。黎明破晓时分，牧羊人不请自来了。“我有好消息要告诉你们。”他脱口而出。

paragraphs.en: I asked, "What is it?" He replied, "My daughter saw your spared bull yesterday. She laughed because she believes he's actually your son, under a spell by his stepmother.
paragraphs.zh: 我问道：“出了什么事？”他回答说：“我女儿昨天看到了你那只留下的公牛。她笑个不停，因为她认为那头公牛其实是你的儿子，被继母施了魔法。”

paragraphs.en: She cried for his mother, who was slaughtered by her father."
paragraphs.zh: 她为她的母亲哭泣，那位母亲被父亲杀害了。

paragraphs.en: The shepherd couldn't wait to share this with me and my wife.
paragraphs.zh: 牧羊人迫不及待地要把这个消息告诉我和我的妻子。

paragraphs.en: Upon hearing this, Demon fainted. When she regained consciousness, she went to her son and fell at his feet, kissing him and weeping. Her son turned towards her, tears streaming down his face, as if pleading for understanding.
paragraphs.zh: 听到这话，恶魔晕了过去。等她苏醒过来，便奔向儿子，跪倒在地，亲吻着他，泪水如泉涌般流下，仿佛在乞求他的理解。

paragraphs.en: She then approached the shepherd’s daughter and offered all her cattle and possessions in exchange for her son's release from the spell.
paragraphs.zh: 她随后走近牧羊女，并提出用自己所有的牲畜和财物来交换，以解救她的儿子。

paragraphs.en: The shepherd’s daughter smiled and proposed two conditions: first, that she be allowed to marry Demon’s son; second, that she cast a spell on the woman who had put the curse on him. Demon agreed, stating that her possessions were now hers and her son's, but her wife would face the consequences of her actions.
paragraphs.zh: 牧羊女微笑着提出了两个条件：首先，她希望允许自己嫁给恶魔之子；其次，她要施法解除那个给他下诅咒的女人的魔咒。恶魔答应了她的要求，表示从今以后她的财产和儿子都归她所有，但她的妻子将为自己的行为承担后果。

paragraphs.en: The shepherd’s daughter then filled a bowl with water, uttered an incantation, and addressed Demon’s son: "Bull, if you have been created by the All Conquering Lord, stay as you are. But if you were treacherously put under a spell, change back to your human form by God's will." She sprinkled him with the water, and he shook himself before transforming from a bull into his human form.
paragraphs.zh: 牧羊女随后盛满一 Bowl 水，念了一句咒语，对魔的儿子说道：“公牛啊，如果你是由全能征服主创造的，请你保持原样。但如果你是被诡计施了魔法，就请在上帝的意愿下恢复为人形吧。”她用这水洒了他一身，只见他抖了抖身子，便从一头公牛变成了人的模样。

paragraphs.en: As I rushed to him, he fainted and regained consciousness just as my wife—the very deer—told me what she had done to his mother. I declared, "Son, God has sent us someone who will repay her for our suffering." Then, to my son, I married the shepherd’s daughter, who transformed my wife into a deer, saying it was better than enduring her sinister looks.
paragraphs.zh: 当我冲过去时，他恰好昏厥又苏醒过来，而我的妻子——那头 Deer 女士，正告诉我她对他的母亲所做的事情。我脱口而出：“儿子，上帝派来了一个要为我们报偿她的人。”然后，我对儿子说，我要将牧羊人的女儿嫁给他，这位牧羊人的女儿将我的妻子变成了一头 Deer，她说这样比忍受她那阴险的眼神要好得多。

paragraphs.en: The years passed with the deer by our side until the shepherd's daughter died. My son then traveled to this man's country, and I set out to find him, stopping here.
paragraphs.zh: 直到牧羊人的女儿去世，那些年月都在鹿的陪伴下悄悄流逝。随后我的儿子前往这个国家，我便踏上寻子之路，最终来到了这里。

paragraphs.en: The demon agreed, granting me one-third of his life. Next, another old man approached, asking if he could tell a stranger story for the same reward. The king consented, and the old man began his tale as dawn broke, interrupting Shahrazad's narrative.
paragraphs.zh: 恶魔答应了，给了我他寿命的三分之一。接着，另一位老人走过来，询问是否可以为同样的报酬给陌生人讲一个故事。国王同意了，老人在黎明时分开始了他的讲述，打断了沙赫拉兹的故事。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad continued her story on the sixth night, saying to King Shahrayar, "If you spare me, I will tell you more tomorrow." The king vowed not to let her die until he heard about the second old man and his dogs.
paragraphs.zh: 莎赫拉兹在第六个夜晚继续讲述她的故事，对国王沙哈雷亚尔说：“如果您饶恕我，我会明天再给您讲更多。”国王发誓，除非听到了第二个老人和他的狗的故事，否则不会让她死去。

paragraphs.en: The first old man begins his tale with a description of the four-day Muslim festival, known for its pilgrimage to Mecca. He explains how it involves sacrificing sheep and cattle as offerings to Allah during this celebration.
paragraphs.zh: 第一个老人的故事从描述为期四天的穆斯林节日开始，这个节日以朝圣者前往麦加而闻名。他解释说，在这次庆祝活动中，人们会献祭羊和牛作为对真主的祭品。
